predecessors.name: Kingdom of Scotland
predecessors.text: the lands John of Islay held from Edward Balliol in 1336, 'the territories which the Islay lords had acquired in the days of Robert I'

successors.name: Kingdom of Scotland
successors.text: 'In 1493, the Parliament of King James IV of Scotland finally brought the independent Lordship of the Isles to an end'; the Crown annexed Islay and the other isles in 1540

ledger.x: 1336: John of Islay becomes 'lord of the isles (1336-1386)'.
1350: 'John was given Robert's daughter Margaret Stewart in marriage, and received Knapdale and Kintyre as dowry' (Robert, later Robert II).
1376: the charters 'granted Lochaber to John and his Stewart wife together' (Robert II section).
1438: Ross and Skye are held with the Hebrides.
mid-1470s: 'John was summoned before parliament to answer for his treasons, and when he failed to appear was declared forfeit.'
1476: 'He lost the earldom of Ross - with the Isle of Skye - as well as Knapdale and Kintyre' but 'retained control of the Hebrides'.
1493: 'In 1493, the Parliament of King James IV of Scotland finally brought the independent Lordship of the Isles to an end.'

wars.name: Forfeiture of Ross and the Lordship
wars.outcome: John summoned before parliament in the mid-1470s, declared forfeit, and in 1476 lost the earldom of Ross with Skye, Knapdale and Kintyre but kept the Hebrides; the Lordship itself was forfeit in 1493.

certainty.note: The pages give lands by name, not boundaries; the shapes are circles round the named islands and glens.

sources.title: John of Islay, Lord of the Isles
